chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali from Ahmad ibn Hilal and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr and Umayyah ibn 'Ali al-Qaysi from 'Ali ibn 'Atiyyah from Zurarah from one of the Imams (peace be upon him)

regarding the Muhrim (one in Ihram), he said to him that he should cover his head and face if he wants to sleep. Therefore, the face in this report is to be understood as referring to the state of necessity, in which a person fears harm from uncovering the head, rather than the state of choice.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on covering the head and face for a Muhrim while sleeping?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani’s al-Ishtibār, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, addresses the permissibility of covering the head and face during Ihram. The scholar interprets the covering of the face not as a general prohibition but as a concession for necessity (ḍarūrah), distinguishing it from voluntary actions to avoid harm. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of easing restrictions when genuine need arises, aligning with the broader legal theory of removing hardship.
